classification.method: fixed host: every load is a new process (cold); no restore exists; warm = the same process's later requests

conclusion: FIXED HOST, NOT LAMBDA. 0xd40 local-file: load 8.085 -> 2.432 s (-5.668 s, 6/6 rounds, p1 range 0.447); memfd -5.677 s (range 0.213). Warm, first inference, 4,096-token forward and peak RSS no change. Answers bit-identical to the same run's P1 and to P1's 0xd40 reference (60/60 requests, 12/12 forwards). x86_64: KleidiAI cannot be compiled, so the change is not in the binary path; every metric no change, answers identical to x86 P1 (30/30, 6/6). Dormant (patched libs, switch unset): load +0.062 s inside p1's 0.447 s range, answers identical. Verdict: general default, with threads = the engine's thread count (the shipped value 6 matched THREADS=6 here).

conditions.note: FIXED HOST, NOT LAMBDA LATENCY. One fresh container per load; arms interleaved in reversal-paired random orders (run_ladder.schedule: each arm before its control in exactly half the rounds); page cache primed before round 0; comparisons pair rounds (arm minus p1 in the same round).

cost.note: fixed host already provisioned; no AWS calls

functions.note: memory_mb is P1's Lambda setting, kept for the schema; the container has no memory limit (cgroup memory.max as recorded per load)

hypothesis: Six-thread KleidiAI load-time repack (GGML_KLEIDIAI_REPACK_THREADS=6) removes the serial repack cost off Lambda too, with no warm/forward/memory or answer change, and is inert where KleidiAI is absent (x86_64).
